title: Carlsen, So, Niemann Take Center Stage As 'Grandmasters' Hits U.S. Theaters
summary: Grandmasters, the documentary offering an inside look at GMs Magnus Carlsen, Wesley So, Hans Niemann, and the struggle over chess's future, has reached movie theaters across the United States. The film screened at 92 AMC locations on October 11 and 14 with a sold-out New York premiere. The theatrical debut and local chess events elicited positive reactions from critics and viewers. Our beloved game has gotten another boost, and this time it's on the big screen. After a packed Tribeca Festival premiere on June 7, the documentary is now reaching more fans through an expanding theatrical run. Grandmasters centers on German entrepreneur Jan Henric Buettner's effort to reshape elite chess alongside Carlsen through Freestyle Chess. The cameras follow the ambitions, negotiations, and clashes with FIDE, while also offering an intimate look at the lives of the top players themselves. So's family life and Niemann's efforts to build his career also offer other perspectives on a world usually seen through tournament broadcasts and results. Directed by Liza Mandelup and produced by Boardwalk Pictures, the studio behind Welcome to Wrexham, Cheer, and Chef's Table, Grandmasters was originally made as a three-part series. The first episode premiered at the Tribeca Festival in June, but the theatrical version brings all three chapters together in a 170-minute film. A centerpiece of the launch was the sold-out October 11 screening at AMC Empire 25 in Times Square, New York. After the screening, Mandelup joined Chess.com CCO IM Danny Rensch and IM Levy Rozman, known to millions as GothamChess, for a live audience Q&A. Mandelup said she kept thinking about Succession while making the documentary. She had been absorbed by the show even though she knew little about the world it depicted, and wanted to create a similar experience for viewers of Grandmasters: "How do you get locked in but also not need to know everything about chess?" Rozman noted how the players appeal beyond their games. "The top of chess is such a fascinating place," he said, describing its leading players as "odd geniuses." He pointed to their different hobbies, languages, and lives around the world as a source of stories beyond the board. At its New York screening, Rensch noted how chess needs more support for telling the stories behind the game and bringing its personalities to a wider audience. "These characters are worth your follow and worth your interest," he said. These characters are worth your follow and worth your interest.—Daniel Rensch Rensch pointed to the potential for players such as So and GM Fabiano Caruana to connect with audiences through more than their moves. "Fans want to show up and hear Wesley So just like they are hearing Levy Rozman right now. They wanna show up and hear Fabi." Have you seen Grandmasters yet??? Help chess go mainstream: Check it out and write a review! 🍿 https://t.co/prMeHoqIGE The film has drawn enthusiastic and positive reactions from some early viewers. Out of 15 audience reviews on the movie review site RottenTomatoes, nine gave it 5/5 stars. Reviewer Nicole praised its "Terrific suspense, intriguing characters, fabulous musical score!" Another viewer called it "Very informative and lots of fun." In a review on Letterboxd, user "Collin" wrote: "This captured the full spectrum of people in the world of chess so beautifully." The release also gave several local chess clubs a chance to meet over the board before heading to the movies. Alongside the New York sellout, these gatherings show how a chess documentary can bring people together. Fans had an opportunity to watch the game's popular figures on screen and make an evening of chess with their own communities. Ahead of the release, Mandelup told Chess.com's State of Chess show: "I love the challenge of people thinking the chess world is boring." Grandmasters is currently showing exclusively at AMC theaters in the United States, but additional locations are set to join the run. Visit the official website for the latest theaters and showtimes, and stay tuned to Chess.com for a full announcement on streaming availability.

title: Movahed Returns To Familiar Freestyle Friday First Position
summary: GM Sina Movahed won Freestyle Friday on October 16, riding a 7/7 start to sole first place on nine points. GM Haowen Xue finished second with 8.5/11, surpassing GM Ian Nepomniachtchi on tiebreaks. The win was Movahed's sixth in Freestyle Friday, tied for the second-most ever, albeit his first victory since January 30 and his first of the Freestyle Friday Championship (FFC) that began in February. GM Maxime Vachier-Lagrave streamed his tournament for Freestyle Chess, finishing ninth, good enough to tack on a point in the FFC standings. Watch the stream back here: GM Magnus Carlsen was also among the participants. After a first-round upset loss, he recovered to 3/4, one of 20 people on that score. GM Anna Muzychuk had 3.5 points, and five players tied for the lead: Movahed, Vachier-Lagrave, GM Christopher Yoo, GM Felix Ilinca, and NM Ethan Sheehan. Only Movahed would reach 5/5, defeating Ilinca while Yoo and Vachier-Lagrave made a draw with each other, as did Sheehan and Carlsen.

title: Maghsoodloo Takes Two 3 0 Thursdays, Caruana Wins 3rd
summary: GM Parham Maghsoodloo won the first two 3 0 Thursday tournaments on October 15, the first player to win consecutive events since GM Jose Martinez did it in back-to-back weeks in March and April. Maghsoodloo tried to become the first player to ever sweep all three Thursday tournaments. However, he struggled in the third tournament, while GM Fabiano Caruana won the event. It's been a fruitful week for Caruana, who won Titled Tuesday and is currently tied for the lead in the U.S. Championship. It took tiebreaks in the end, but Maghsoodloo left little doubt that he deserved first place in the opening tournament of the day. He won his first seven games, capped off by a sudden tactic against the tournament's top seed, GM Hikaru Nakamura.

title: SLU, UTD, Texas Tech Still Perfect In Collegiate Chess League
summary: The last two league champions, Saint Louis University (SLU) and the University of Texas at Dallas (UTD), are the two undefeated teams after two matches each in the 2026 fall season of the Collegiate Chess League. SLU has dominated both matches that it has played, defeating the University of Texas at Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV) and the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC). Meanwhile, UTD had a narrow victory against the SRM Institute of Science and Technology and a convincing win against UTRGV. CCL Division 1 Standings SLU has played just two matches in the fall season so far, and hasn't been challenged, winning with a combined score of 28.5/32. Its most recent match against UMBC saw the team sweep the final three rounds to finish with a 13.5-2.5 victory. GM Francesco Sonis led the way, scoring a perfect 4-0. His game against IM Adam Frank featured a smooth endgame victory.

title: One move can change everything in the World Championships U7-U17
summary: With six rounds completed and five to go, every half-point counts as the race for the world titles intensifies in Roquetas de Mar, Spain. As the 2026 World U7-U17 Chess Championships reaches the halfway point, the tension is mounting across all age categories. With six rounds completed and five still to play, every half-point matters, and the pressure is becoming increasingly evident as young players face the challenge of balancing ambition with nerves. Some have established commanding leads, while others find themselves in tightly packed groups where a single mistake could dramatically change the standings. Rating favourites are fighting to stay in contention, and emerging talents are seizing their opportunities on the world stage. With Round 7 approaching after a well-deserved rest day, the players will return to the boards knowing that the final stretch is drawing closer and that the margin for error is shrinking with every move. Let’s take a closer look at each age group. Under 7 (53 players in the open section and 28 players in the girls’ section) A three-way tie at the top of the Under-7 girls’ standings sees Margad Bayasgalan of Mongolia, Leila Aldazharova of Kazakhstan, and Echo Heming Fang, representing Canada, all on 5/6, with five rounds still to play. Two of the three leaders have already suffered a defeat, while Aldazharova has drawn twice – a relatively rare occurrence in the Under-7 section, where decisive games are the norm. In the Open section, Poland’s Ignacy Mongay Miland (pictured above) is setting the pace with a perfect six out of six. He holds a full-point lead over Egypt’s Mohab Ahmed Assem, with a further seven players just behind on 4.5/6. The seventh round will see the two leaders face each other in a potentially pivotal encounter. There is still a long way to go, but a positive result for Mongay Miland would strengthen his position considerably as he looks to maintain his perfect score. Top seed Stella Zhu of Finland is among three players on 4.5/6, keeping the pressure on the leaders as the tournament progresses. Mate of the day  Symbat Otargali – Varvara Volkova One of the most striking tactical moments came in the third round, when Varvara Volkova found a neat three-move forced checkmate. Her combination began with the spectacular 28…Rf1+!, followed by 29.Rxf1 Qxf1+ 30.Qxf1 Rxf1#. Black’s precise execution secured an important point. The Open section has two co-leaders on 5.5/6, with a third player just half a point behind. Latvia’s Akims Jefimovs holds a slight tiebreak advantage over Uzbekistan’s Sayfuddin Erkinboev, while Estonia’s Lev Jevglevski remains firmly in contention on 5/6. With the leaders separated by such narrow margins, the next rounds could prove decisive in shaping the race for the title. Standings after Round 6 – Open U9 Standings after Round 6 – Girls U9 Under 11 (99 players in the open section and 47 players in the girls’ section) Uzbekistan’s Akbar Mustafakulov leads the Under-11 Open section with an impressive 5.5/6, half a point ahead of a group of five players on 5/6. The 2026 Asian Champion has displayed solid fundamentals throughout the opening six rounds, dropping just half a point so far. Among his closest pursuers is top seed Amirzhan Anetov of Kazakhstan, a Candidate Master who remains firmly in the title race. In the Girls’ section, Kazakhstan’s Women Candidate Master Milana Filippova (pictured below) is setting the pace with a perfect six out of six. She holds a full-point lead over Georgia’s Sara Saltkhutsishvili, whom she has already defeated, giving her a valuable advantage in the race for the title. Filippova has already demonstrated her strength at continental level, winning the Under-10 Asian Championship in 2025. She will now look to maintain her winning streak as the tournament enters its next phase. Standings after Round 6 – Open U11 Standings after Round 6 – Girls U11 Under 13 (75 players in the open section and 43 players in the girls’ section) Women Candidate Master Lilian Schirmbeck of Germany leads the Under-13 Girls’ section with 5/6, having recorded four wins and two draws. She holds a half-point advantage over a group of six players on 4.5/6, including several of the other rating favourites. With the standings still tightly packed, the battle for the title remains wide open. In the Open section, Egypt’s International Master Abdalrahman Sameh Mohamed (pictured below) has made a perfect start, winning all six of his games. His next challenge promises to be a major test, as he faces Kazakhstan’s International Master Danis Kuandykuly, the rating favourite, who has dropped just one draw so far. Sameh arrives at this crucial encounter with an impressive recent achievement to his name: victory in the 2025 FIDE World Cup in the Under-12 category. With both players among the strongest competitors in the field, their meeting could prove a pivotal moment in the race for the title. Kazakhstan’s FIDE Master Aldiyar Zharas currently leads with 5.5/6, but the pressure is mounting, with no fewer than five titled players just half a point behind on 5/6. Among them is Spain’s FIDE Master Martin Krauchi Romero, who remains firmly in contention as the battle for the top places intensifies. The Girls’ section is equally competitive, with three players sharing the lead on 5/6. title: Review: The Modern Benko Gambit - A Full Repertoire Against 1.d4 by GM Sipke Ernst
summary:
In modern chess, activity has become one of the most valuable resources of all. In recent years, the popular Benko Gambit has come under considerable theoretical pressure: in particular, the critical White line with 12.a4 posed extremely difficult problems for Black and seemed to rob the opening of its dynamic potential.

A look at the repertoire:

With a total running time of approximately three hours, the Dutch grandmaster demonstrates that the Benko Gambit is perfectly suited to the modern computer era. Rather than drifting into the typical manoeuvring positions associated with 1.d4 , Black forces the opponent into sharp, double-edged play right from the start. The repertoire is divided into the following sections:

The new main line: After 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 c5 3.d5 b5 4.cxb5 a6 5.bxa6 , Sipke Ernst unveils the novelty 5...e6! :

Ernst provides a detailed analysis of the critical 6.dxe6 as well as the highly complex and exciting positions arising after 6.Nc3 exd5 7.Nxd5 Be7 . White's traditional attempt to cling to the extra pawn is met with uncompromising central activity.

White's alternatives on move 5: Ernst provides precise antidotes to the solid 5.e3 , including sharp analysis after 5...Bb7 6.Nc3 axb5 7.Bxb5 Qa5 , as well as against all sidelines, including 5.Nc3, 5.b6 and the ambitious 5.f3 .

Early deviations on moves 3 and 4: The course covers all of White's attempts to decline the pawn sacrifice, including 4.a4, 4.Nd2, 4.Qc2 and 4.Nf3 , as well as 3.dxc5 or 3.Nf3 .

A major strength of this course is its pragmatic and comprehensive approach. Ernst offers complete systems against 2.Nf3 and provides full coverage of popular Queen's Pawn openings such as the London System, the Trompowsky Attack and the Richter-Veresov Attack.

Black thus gets an all-in-one repertoire against 1.d4 .

As we have come to expect from ChessBase, the video material is complemented by an extensive range of learning tools. The course runs across platforms in the FritzTrainer app for Windows and Mac, is available as a download or CB Book, and can also be streamed conveniently via the ChessBase video portal.

Throughout the videos, Ernst regularly presents the user with key positions. After the user enters a move, the author either praises the correct plan or explains clearly through video feedback why an incorrect attempt fails. Using the Fritz Online web app, newly learned positions can immediately be put to the test in training games against Fritz. The Opening web app also allows users to play through complex variations using Autoplay and memorise them systematically until the move sequences become second nature.

The interface allows users to enter their own variations at any time or activate any locally installed engine for in-depth analysis, supported by useful features such as LiveBook and Assisted Analysis.

The package includes comprehensive databases of illustrative games and repertoire variations. All of GM Sipke Ernst's analyses can be saved directly to the user's personal digital opening repertoire. With the help of the Opening Reference, users can play through the variations on the analysis board, examine them and compare them with current grandmaster practice. Replay Training also helps improve their understanding of the resulting middlegame structures.

Conclusion

The Modern Benko Gambit is a milestone for all Benko Gambit players. Sipke Ernst succeeds in thoroughly modernising the gambit with his exciting new approach based on 5...e6 . Anyone who no longer wants to defend passively against 1.d4 , but instead wants to put White under sustained, dynamic pressure right from the start, should not miss this course.

***

About the author:

Sipke Ernst, born in 1979, is a Dutch chess grandmaster and FIDE Trainer. He earned the grandmaster title in 2007 and reached his peak Elo rating of 2606 in January 2012.

Ernst won three bronze medals at the Dutch Chess Championship and finished runner-up in 2017 after a playoff. He also represented the Netherlands at the 2002 Chess Olympiad and the 2009 European Team Championship. Today, he works primarily as a professional chess coach and produces training courses for ChessBase.

title: Dortmund Sparkassen Trophy 2027
summary:
By moving to the Salzlager, the tournament not only gains a new, striking venue, but also the opportunity to expand its capacity. Up to 450 active participants are expected at the Sparkassen Chess Trophy 2027. In doing so, the organiser, Initiative Pro Schach e.V., is sending a clear signal regarding the further development of Dortmund as a centre for chess.

Chess meets the Garden Show: a festival with something extra to offer

Being part of the 2027 International Garden Exhibition opens up new opportunities for the Chess Days. All active tournament participants will automatically be granted access to the IGA site for the duration of their participation. This makes the Sparkassen Chess Trophy a special experience that goes beyond the chessboard, combining sport, socialising and cultural experiences.

About the IGA 2027 in the Ruhr region

Under the theme ‘How do we want to live tomorrow?’, the 2027 International Garden Exhibition will present innovative solutions to future challenges in green infrastructure and urban development in the Ruhr region on an international stage and across three levels. The ‘GARDENS OF THE FUTURE’ section also provides the backdrop for presentations on horticulture, landscaping and plant production. The IGA Gardens of the Future are currently being created in Dortmund, Duisburg, Gelsenkirchen, Lünen and the Emscherland region.

Other local authorities in the Ruhr region are showcasing the region’s green treasures in the ‘OUR GARDENS’ section. The ‘MY GARDEN’ section gives residents the opportunity to get involved through private initiatives and collaborations. The International Garden Exhibition, featuring around 6,000 events, will take place from 23 April to 17 October 2027 – for the first time not in a single city, but across the entire metropolitan region. A total of around 3.1 million visitors are expected.

"Chess captivates people all over the world – across generations and national borders. We are therefore all the more delighted to welcome the International Dortmund Chess Days to the IGA 2027. Whether you’re sitting at the board yourself or cheering on the grandmasters as they play, this festival brings the fascination of chess to life for many people. With the salt warehouse as the venue and the blossoming ‘Garden of the Future’ right on the doorstep, chess fans can look forward to an extraordinary setting for their sport. This will be a wonderful addition to the Chess Days and to our IGA,” says Hanspeter Faas, spokesperson for the management board of IGA 2027 Ruhr."

From grandmasters to ambitious amateurs: chess for everyone

The concept of the International Dortmund Chess Days as a chess festival will remain central to the event in 2027. International grandmasters, top German players and ambitious club players will come together with chess enthusiasts from Germany and abroad. The blend of top-class competitive chess and an open, cross-generational field of participants is what gives the event its special character.

A key advantage of the new venue is that all open tournaments can be held simultaneously in the shared playing hall. This not only creates ideal organisational conditions but also emphasises the communal festival experience. Spectators can look forward to the popular live commentary on the top matches taking place on site again in 2027.

A special partnership for a special year in chess

Christian Jochmann, Managing Director of the organising body, Pro Schach e.V., is very much looking forward to the collaboration:

"Our partnership with the IGA 2027 is an exceptional opportunity for us. We are bringing the fascination of chess to a special venue, whilst at the same time opening up our festival to even more people.This is a major coup for our event and for Dortmund as a sporting hub. We look forward to working with our partners to organise a chess festival that will reach far beyond the chess community."

Further information on the 54th International Dortmund Chess Days will be published around the turn of the year. The specific tournament formats, the official announcements and the registration options are due to be announced then. Chess enthusiasts from Germany and abroad can therefore now mark the date in their diaries and look forward to further details about the chess festival as part of the IGA 2027.

Further information will be available at www.sparkassen-chess-trophy.de .
